• the horse’s bridle/halter hardware (buckles, stitching, leather thickness)  
• the woman’s hand and fingers (shape, count, joint placement)  
• subtle texture transitions in coat, mane and background bokeh  

Below are zoom-ins of those areas for all four candidates:

1. First image – The fingers look slightly rubbery; the leather strap’s stitching fades abruptly and the metal ring has a faint “melting” artifact.

Look first at the outer surface that is printed on the piece of card,

.  
It is a circle that has been divided into four separate quarter-discs by a vertical and a horizontal cut.  
Because the four quarters are still attached to each other along those two cuts, the only sensible way to “fold” the piece is to hinge the quarters about the two straight cuts:

1. Fold the two upper quarters (NW and NE) upward through 90°.  
2. Fold the two lower quarters (SW and SE) downward through 90°.

After the fold:

• The two upper quarters meet edge-to-edge and create one complete semicircle that opens upward.  
• The two lower quarters meet edge-to-edge and create a second complete semicircle that opens downward.  

Those two semicircles touch each other along their common straight edge, producing the unmistakable “hour-glass” outline shown in the answer set.

Because every quarter keeps its own dots, the exact pattern of black-filled and white-hollow dots that was in the NW quarter ends up on the left half of the upper semicircle, the dots from the NE quarter end up on the right half of the upper semicircle, and so on.  
Comparing the four alternatives, only picture B shows:

• Two opposite semicircles touching along one straight edge.  
• The hollow (white) dots lying in exactly the same places that the original quarters carry once they have been rotated into their new positions.

Pictures A, C and D either keep the shape flat (A) or swap/rotate the quarters in ways that could never result from the single 90° “hinge” folds described above (C and D).

Therefore the only figure that can be produced by folding the given outer surface is

(B)  picture B
